Barbour and Levi’s are collaborating on some upcycled jeans

Barbour and Levi’s Japan are giving vintage 501s a second life with waxed cotton, tartan and corduroy from Barbour’s archive.

BY

Karen Carillo
09th Sep 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:13
Instaread

A worn pair of Levi’s 501s can already look like it has lived a few lives, but Barbour and Levi’s Japan are giving some of them one more.

The new Levi’s x Barbour Re-Loved collection turns vintage 501s into one-off jeans using reclaimed denim alongside Barbour waxed cotton, tartan and wide-wale corduroy. Every pair is assembled individually, so the patches, wear and materials will differ from one to the next.

Both brands have spent years encouraging repair and longer wear, so rebuilding old pieces feels more natural than creating an entirely new collaboration from scratch.

Old 501s get the Barbour treatment

The starting point is a used pair of Levi’s 501s, but sections of the original denim are replaced or supplemented with fabrics more often found on a Barbour jacket.

Waxed cotton brings some of the rugged texture associated with the British brand, while tartan and chunky corduroy add further contrast. The existing signs of wear are left as part of the finished piece, meaning the jeans are not being made to look fresh from the factory.

Advertisement

This is not the first time Barbour has found a new use for old clothing. Its Re-Loved programme normally takes unwanted wax jackets, cleans and repairs them where needed, rewaxes the fabric and puts the garments back into circulation. This collaboration takes that idea further by bringing in vintage Levi’s denim and duck cloth, giving materials from both brands another life.

As Hypebeast explains, no two pairs are identical because everything is made from collected and reused fabric. A faded patch of denim or a worn section of waxed cotton becomes part of what separates one pair from another.

Going beyond jeans

Barbour Japan is also producing Re-Loved jackets for the collection. These start with Barbour’s waxed outerwear and bring pieces of Levi’s denim into the reconstruction.

The interesting part is seeing what happens when the two brands start borrowing from each other’s wardrobes. Levi’s denim finds its way onto Barbour jackets, while waxed cotton, tartan and corduroy are stitched into the 501s. It gives the collection a much more obvious crossover than a simple logo swap.

Alongside the clothing, the two brands are releasing something a little smaller. Sets of pins inspired by archive designs from both companies will also be available as part of the collection.

Advertisement

Every pair really is limited

As for pricing, the Re-Loved 501 is set at ¥38,500 in Japan (approx. $250), while Barbour lists the collaborative Re-Loved jackets at ¥94,600 (approx. $617). The pin sets cost ¥8,800 (approx. $57). All three arrive on September 11.

Levi’s will offer the jeans through its Harajuku flagship, with customers entering a lottery for purchasing order on launch morning. Barbour Japan also lists a small number of the jeans at its Harajuku Cat Street store, with purchases limited to one of each item per person while stocks last.

For two brands with products that often look better once they have picked up a few years of wear, throwing the old material away would almost miss the point. These 501s keep those marks and repairs visible, then add pieces from another equally well-worn wardrobe staple to make each pair impossible to duplicate.
